notes:
Account summary: Scarlet Haven (mid-market product analytics SaaS). Trialled Redwood Hosted API for 3 weeks to validate chat-based support assistant + doc search embedding pipeline. Positive qualitative results: faster response times vs current hosted provider, embeddings recall good for KB. Primary asks: predictable SLA, VPC network controls, and unit economics for 6-12 month growth.

Trial telemetry (hosted API):
- Avg daily requests: 18k (peak day 42k)
- Avg tokens / request (chat + synth): 420 tokens (median 210)
- Token mix observed: ~60% short interactions (<128 tokens), ~30% medium (128-512), ~10% long (>512).
- Embeddings: 28k embedding units/day (batch jobs at 03:00 UTC), average vector dim 1536.
- Observed P95 latency (hosted): 230ms for short chat requests, 720ms for medium; long batches run async.
- Error rate during trial: 0.6% (mostly quota throttles during peak bursts).

Sizing ask (from Scarlet Haven engineering): forecast to replace hosted with Dedicated in Q2 once network + legal greenlight. Requested: recommended Dedicated pool size with clear QPS/concurrency and fallback plan.

Redwood SE recommended baseline Dedicated configurations (costed options):
1) Conservative - SM throughput: 2 x A10G nodes (ops: steady-state 2-3 QPS, bursts to 8 QPS), target concurrency 8, reserved for 24/7 support assistant and nightly embedding jobs. Expected monthly token volume: ~45M tokens. Estimated ARR contribution: $75k/year.
2) Production - Perf throughput: 4 x A10G (or 2 x A100 80GB) (sustained 6-10 QPS, burst-friendly to 20 QPS), concurrency budget 20, KV prefix cache enabled for chat to reduce token costs by ~15%. Supports live personalization and real-time reranking. Expected monthly token volume: ~120M tokens. Estimated ARR: $140k-$180k/year.
3) Growth - High-availability: 2x perf pools cross-region + autoscale (for EU/NA fallbacks). Provisioning assumes 99.9% availability and cross-region fallback routing. Intended for customers with strict residency + SLA. Estimated ARR: $200k+.

POC notes / engineering findings:
- Token mix drives CPU/GPU time more than raw QPS; caching short chat phrases reduced repeat tokens by ~12% during trial.
- Embedding batch windows can be moved to off-peak to reduce concurrency strain; recommended scheduled windows 02:00-05:00 UTC.
- Network: Scarlet Haven requires VPC peering + dedicated NAT egress; ops requested template for routing and least-privilege SGs.
- Security: SOC2 + SSO/SAML are mandatory; legal requested Redwood DPA + encryption-at-rest details; KMS support required for Private later.

Quotes / stakeholder snippets:
- VP Product: "If we can get predictable latency under load and a clear per-token runway, we can sign for Dedicated next quarter."
- Head of Infra: "Need concrete network playbook and a test window for VPC peering before we flip prod traffic."
